snip.t: Coronary angiography - usually performed when coronary artery bypass graft surgery or percutaneous coronary intervention is being considered.

Percutaneous Coronary Intervention- involves passing a guidewire across a coronary stenosis under radiographic control, and using it to position a balloon that is then inflated to dilate the stenosis.
Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI): A catheter is used to mechanically open the blocked artery, often with stent placement.
STEMI: Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) — Intravenous fibrinolysis

qs.q: Why do drug-eluting stents necessitate prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary interventions?
o: They completely prevent venous stasis within the deep veins of the lower extremities
They promote the rapid proliferation of HHV8-associated vascular neoplasms locally
They delay reendothelialisation, significantly increasing the risk of late stent thrombosis
They induce severe chronic lymphedema and subcutaneous brawny induration changes
qs.e: Drug-eluting stents significantly reduce restenosis but delay reendothelialisation, requiring prolonged dual antiplatelet therapy to prevent catastrophic late stent thrombosis. The incorrect options attribute entirely unrelated clinical and pathological consequences to stent placement.
